# Analysis {#sec-analysis}

```{r}
#| label: setup-analysis
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tinytable)
options(tinytable_html_mathjax = TRUE)

here::i_am("manuscript/_quarto.yml")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
targets::tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets"),
  script = here::here("_targets.R")
)

targets::tar_load(c(
  penguins_clean,
  analysis_body_mass,
  analysis_flipper_fit
))
invisible(list2env(targets::tar_read(fn_figure), .GlobalEnv))
theme_set(theme_proj())
```

Figures are built inline from pipeline targets with ggplot; they are never registered as targets or written to disk.
@fig-flipper-fit shows the example pattern, with data and fitted lines distinguished in the legend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-flipper-fit
#| fig-cap: "Body mass and flipper length by species"
#| fig-notes: "Palmer penguins, observations with recorded sex and body mass. Lines are species-specific linear fits."
ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = penguins_clean,
    aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass, color = sex, shape = sex),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = analysis_flipper_fit$pred,
    aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass, group = species),
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  scale_sex(name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = "Body mass (g)") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.15, 0.9)
  )
```

Tables use `tinytable`, with math in cells written in LaTeX and rewritten for Typst by `theme_mitex()` (@tbl-flipper-fit).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flipper-fit
#| tbl-cap: "Linear fits of body mass on flipper length"
analysis_flipper_fit$coef |>
  mutate(across(c(intercept, slope, r2), \(x) sprintf("%.2f", x))) |>
  setNames(c("Species", "Intercept", "Slope", "$R^2$")) |>
  tt(notes = notes_text("OLS fits by species on the sample of @fig-flipper-fit.")) |>
  theme_mitex()
```
